label: Original-phase input of 1/p/j/q/3/u/2/v/h/c after r/w/l/a/x/e/z/o earlier
explanation: Mostly fires in the original (input) phase (85% of mass), peaking around t=2-3 and at late positions of long sequences. Driven by the current input token: 1 is strongest (30% rate, 21% of mass, includes most top activations), then p, j, q, 3, u, 2, with weaker v/h/c. It is boosted when earlier inputs include r, w, l, a, x, e, z or o (e.g. r l l 1, w e l a 1); first occurrences of the token fire more than repeats. Rarely fires at the delimiter step; copy-phase activity (14% of mass) is weaker and is mostly at recall_idx 1 and on outputs w/r/x. It looks like a graded, additive mix of current-token and history-token contributions, so a boolean predicate captures only part of it: the predicate gets about 0.69 dev mass recall at about 0.31 precision.
